We spent a lot of time building a terminal at Sidestep on top of Stripe (and a few other processors). The hardest part wasn't managing devices, but hardware integration for accepting cards... the ability to fully integrate with the API on a terminal level is the most powerful thing here, especially combined with Stripe Connect.
So far, Stripe seems to have lowered the fixed fee from 30¢ to 5¢ and dropped 0.2% off their payment gateway fees for card-present transactions compared to online.

I am working with a company that has small physical stores processing hundreds of payments every day... having to rely on all the existing crappy hardware for taking payments is a pain in the a$$.. this looks like it could change the game.
We have developed a POS for salons and spa and have been working with various in-store payment solutions - including Square. None of the existing solutions meet our needs.
I had to search for 'Stripe terminal' on Google to get a picture of the real thing as opposed to the picture on the webpage. They don't really look the same. Unless it's a new model.

A developer who built a POS terminal at Sidestep on top of Stripe and other processors said the hardest part was the card-reader hardware integration, not device management. Readers were too expensive and failed too often. They saw full API integration at the terminal level, plus Stripe Connect support (customer swipes card -> your software -> client's bank account), as the most powerful part.
